changes: The percentile interval stays the primary interval for every contrast, as registered.
BCa and t intervals are added as sensitivity analyses for the seven primary contrasts and the decision rule's best-minus-second intervals.
Every reported interval is accompanied by the simulated coverage of its method at the realized episode count, from the file above.
The number of episodes with any call below -1 in each compared quantity is reported, so readers can see whether the rare-extreme regime applies.
reason: The pre-registered coverage check (analysis/revision_gpu/v1/coverage.py, results in analysis/revision_gpu/v1/results/coverage-before-unblinding.json, sha256 4b7a6db7b18c85ac0473282c85ab967128b1adec7eaae8baa8eed9e618b95588) found that percentile episode-bootstrap intervals undercover at 30 to 60 episodes when episode effects are skewed or include rare extreme negative episodes: nominal 95% gave 0.873 to 0.910 (lognormal skew) and 0.759 to 0.880 (5% extreme episodes). No interval type fixed this uniformly: the t interval was best for symmetric heavy tails, BCa for skew and rare extremes at 60 episodes.
